title: Analysis of Commit Signing on GitHub
abstract: arXiv:2604.14014v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Since 1999, the security community has known that managing cryptographic keys is hard for users of cryptographic systems. Git lets software developers use private keys they control to digitally sign the commits that record their code changes to a repository. This practice offers a rare opportunity to study how a large community manages cryptographic keys in everyday work. In this paper, we study end-to-end commit signing, using GitHub accounts as our sampling unit. Our 2% stratified sample of the GitHub population comprises 2,737,649 accounts, 71,694 of which have made at least one commit. For these accounts, we analyze 16,112,439 commits across 874,198 repositories and collect 208,546 public keys uploaded to the sampled accounts. We examine developers' signing key usage patterns and compare our findings with those of prior commit signing studies, most of which used repository-based samples and paid less attention to key management.

translated_abstract: 自1999年以来，安全界就已经知道，对密码学系统的用户而言，管理密码学密钥十分困难。Git允许软件开发者使用自己控制的私钥，对记录代码更改的提交进行数字签名。这一做法为研究大型社区在日常工作中如何管理密码学密钥提供了难得的机会。在本文中，我们以GitHub账户为抽样单位，对提交签名进行了端到端的研究。我们对GitHub用户群体进行了2%的分层抽样，共包含2,737,649个账户，其中71,694个账户至少进行过一次提交。针对这些账户，我们分析了874,198个仓库中的16,112,439次提交，并收集了上传至抽样账户的208,546个公钥。我们考察了开发者签名密钥的使用模式，并将研究结果与以往提交签名研究进行比较——这些研究大多采用基于仓库的抽样方式，且较少关注密钥管理问题。
tldr: 该论文首次以GitHub账户为抽样单位，通过对270多万个账户、1600多万次提交和20多万个公钥的大规模端到端分析，系统揭示了开发者提交签名中签名密钥的使用与管理模式。
en_tdlr: This paper presents the first end-to-end, account-based study of commit signing on GitHub, analyzing over 2.7 million accounts, 16 million commits, and 200 thousand public keys to systematically reveal developers' signing key usage and management patterns.
